messages.subject: Between-group dissimilarity (streamlining for loops)
parts:
Hi, 

I’m interested in the dissimilarity between samples (beta-diversity), and my samples are split into two groups. When I want to know the dissimilarity between samples within a given group, this is a simple call to the function vegdist() from the vegan package, which acts on a matrix and calculates the difference between each sample and every other sample in the group. 

But I also want to know the between-group dissimilarities, as in the difference between each sample in group A and every sample in group B. Right now I’m doing this with nested for loops, but I’m wondering if there’s a more elegant way to do it. Ideally I would like to be able to do this with more than two groups as well. 

braybetween <- numeric()
for (i in 1:length(spA[,1])){   # iterate over each sample in group A
  current <- numeric(length(spB[,1]))  # create a vector to store dissimilarity calculations in for that sample in group A

  for (j in 1:length(spB[,1])){  # iterate over each sample in group B
    current[j] <- vegdist(rbind(spA[i,], spB[j,]))  # dissimilarity between sample i in group A and sample j in group B
    j <- j+1
  }

  braybetween <- c(braybetween, current) # add the dissimilarity calculations for sample i to the total vector of dissimilarities
  i <- i+1
}

Thank you for your thoughts and criticisms! 

~
Chhaya M Werner
PhD Student, UC Davis

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: Between-group dissimilarity (streamlining for loops)
parts:
Hi Chhaya,

First, in R there is no need to manually iterate your index in the loop, so i <- i + 1 is not needed.

Second, the vegdist returns a distance matrix, which means you can calculate the entire matrix and then subset to get the numbers you want rather than calculating each distance separately. If you do this:

result <- vegdist(rbind(spA,spB))

You will get a big matrix (actually a vector, but don't worry about that) that is organized like this:

             spA             spB
          |-------------|-------------|
   spA |               |      X       |
          |-------------|-------------|
   spB |      X       |               |
          |-------------|-------------|

You are interested in one of the areas marked with the X, which is just:

as.matrix(result)[(nrow(spA) + 1):(2 * nrow(spA),1:nrow(spA)]

Assuming nrow(spA) == nrow(spB).

Only word of caution - depending on the size of your matrix, the as.matrix call can eat up your memory. There are cleaver ways of getting around this if you need. 

Hope that helps,

Matt
